text:
Predicates:
Managed(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed in y.
Deposit(x, y) ::: the security deposit for x is y.
Rent(x, y) ::: the monthly rent for x is y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Apartment(x) ::: x is an apartment.
Premises:
∃x (Managed(x) ∧ ∃y (Pet(y) ∧ Allowed(y, x))) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (Managed(x) → ∃y Deposit(x, y)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (Managed(x) → ∀y (Deposit(x, y) → Deposit(x, y) ≥ Rent(x, y))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Pet(fluffy) ::: Cats are pets and Fluffy is Tom's cat.
Managed(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
(Rent(x, y) > 1500) ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
∀x (Managed(x) → (TomRents(x) ↔ (Allowed(fluffy, x) ∧ Deposit(x, y) ≤ 1500))) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
Conclusion:
(Deposit(oliveGarden, 2000) ∨ Deposit(oliveGarden, y)) ∧ (y > 2000) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
